Purpose: To decide from dated data whether a provider may be used at an auth tier for an audience.
Caller and time: Role resolution at launch; the engine at every switch to a fallback; the doctor.
Inputs: `evaluate`: provider, auth tier, audience, acknowledgements of the consumer.
Outputs: The decision and the row it rests on.
Errors: None of its own. No row means unknown terms.
Guarantees of the core: The terms gate is evaluated at launch, at role resolution and at every switch to a fallback. No comment,
flag, mode or project key bypasses it. A front harness is gated by the row of its back end. Auth
tier 3 without an `allowed` row is refused with the explanation.
Guarantees of an implementation: A data file holds, per row: provider, auth tier, audience (`personal`, `distributed`), status
(`allowed`, `conditional`, `personal-only`, `refused`), source, access date, the quoted sentence,
Failure of an implementation: A data file that does not validate is ignored with a doctor finding, and the shipped file applies.
Unknown-value rule: No row: auth tiers 1 and 2 are allowed with a warning, never as a default and never for an
automatic pick. An unknown status is read as `refused`. Data older than 30 days is a doctor
Wave 1 implementations: The data file shipped in the package. A newer file placed in user-level state replaces it.
Content owner: 147. The harness adapters supply the facts of their rows.
Proving test: Table tests generated from the verified terms matrix. A row for a fictional provider in a test
overlay changes the decision with no code change.
